title: Graph DFS / BFS
learn: visited set, connected components, BFS for shortest path in unweighted graphs, bipartite check
hook: Number of Provinces, Clone Graph, Keys and Rooms and Word Ladder are all "just" DFS or BFS with a visited set. Knowing which one to reach for (BFS for fewest steps) is what interviewers check.

explain.prompt: Compare DFS and BFS on a graph: how each works, why you need a visited set, and when BFS gives shortest paths.
keyPoints: both visit every reachable node once with a visited set, O(V + E)
graphs can have cycles, so without a visited set the search never ends
DFS goes deep first (stack/recursion): components, cycles, backtracking
BFS explores by distance (queue): the first time it reaches a node is via the fewest edges
run the search from every unvisited node to count connected components
